# Problem 2 - Tidyverse: Tennis - data.table

```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(data.table)
library(stringr)
```

```{r}
atp_2019_url = paste0(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/azhou5849/tennis-atp-sackmann-data/",
    "refs/heads/master/atp_matches_2019.csv"
)
if (!dir.exists('p2')) dir.create('p2')
if (!file.exists('./p2/atp_matches_2019.csv'))
    download.file(atp_2019_url, './p2/atp_matches_2019.csv')
```

```{r}
atp_2019 <- fread('./p2/atp_matches_2019.csv')
```

How many tournaments took place in 2019?

```{r}
uniqueN(atp_2019$tourney_id)
```

128 tournaments took place in 2019.

Did any player win more than one tournament? If so, how many players won more than one tournament, and how many tournaments did the most winning player(s) win?

```{r}
atp_2019
```

```{r}
multiple_win <- atp_2019[round == "F",
                        .(count = .N),
                        by = winner_name][count > 1][order(-count)]

list(
  win_count = nrow(multiple_win),
  most_winner = multiple_win[count == max(count), winner_name],
  most_winner_wins = max(multiple_win$count)
)
```

12 players won more than one tournament in 2019. Novak Djokovic and Dominic Thiem won the most tournaments, with 5 wins each.

Is there any evidence that winners have more aces than losers? 

```{r}
t.test(
  atp_2019$w_ace,
  atp_2019$l_ace,
  paired = TRUE,
  alternative = "greater"
)
```

Yes, there is strong evidence that winners have more aces than losers on average. The p-value is less than 2.2e-16, which is much smaller than 0.05. On average, winners have about 1.70 more aces than losers.

Identify the player(s) with the highest win-rate. (Note that this is NOT asking for the highest number of wins.) Restrict to players with at least 5 matches.

```{r}
win_count <- atp_2019[, .(win_count = .N), by = .(name = winner_name)]
lose_count <- atp_2019[, .(lose_count = .N), by = .(name = loser_name)]

player_stats <- merge(win_count, lose_count, by = "name", all = TRUE)

player_stats[is.na(win_count), win_count := 0]
player_stats[is.na(lose_count), lose_count := 0]

player_stats[, total_match := win_count + lose_count]
player_stats[, win_rate := win_count / total_match]

eligible <- player_stats[total_match >= 5]
eligible[win_rate == max(win_rate)]
```

Rafael Nadal had the highest win rate of 86.96%. He won 60 out of 69 matches in 2019.
